Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimant has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge, Raichur (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.490/2020 vide its judgment and award dated 28.02.2022.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimant, a junior lineman employed with Gulbarga Electricity Supply Company, suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 02.03.2020 when the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36/EU-5487 ridden by him was involved in an accident with the tractor and trailer unit.

The claimant suffered injuries in the accident and was treated as an inpatient at Manipal Hospital,
Bengaluru, where he underwent a major surgery.
A claim petition was filed by the claimant seeking compensation from the owner and insurer of the tractor and trailer.
The claim petition was resisted by the insurer who denied the accident as well as the entitlement of the claimant for the compensation.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined PW.1.
He marked documents as Exs.P1 to P16.

The insurer did not lead any evidence but marked copy of the insurance policy as Ex.R1.
5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the claimant had suffered bilateral anterior column fracture with bilateral ischiopubic rami fracture.
The Tribunal held that the claimant was employed as junior lineman with Gulbarga Electricity Supply Company and was drawing monthly salary of Rs.33,000/- per month.
The Tribunal held that there was no evidence on record to indicate that the claimant's income was reduced due to the injury.

Since the accident and the injury was proved by the claimant, the Tribunal awarded the following compensation:-

The Tribunal directed the insurer to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
6. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal.

7. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that though the claimant was not entitled to any compensation for loss of income due to disability as he was employed but yet, the compensation awarded under the other heads was meager and warrants enhancement.
8. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer submitted that the claimant did not produce any evidence to indicate that he had availed any leave during the period of treatment.

He also contended that since the claimant did not suffer any loss of income, the Tribunal was justified in not NC:
2023:KHC-K:5562 awarding any compensation towards the same.
He further contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the insurer.
10. It is evident from the records that the claimant had suffered major fracture to the anterior column with bilateral ischiopubic rami fracture.

The claimant was a junior lineman meaning thereby that he was required to climb poles and fracture of the anterior column with bilateral ischiopubic rami fracture would certainly affect his duties as a junior lineman.

However, since there is no material on record to indicate that the claimant had suffered any loss of income due to the injury suffered, the Tribunal was justified in not awarding any compensation towards it.
However, the Tribunal must have awarded just compensation for the loss of amenities and under other heads.

In that view of the matter, without going into the minute details of the case, this Court considers it appropriate to enhance the compensation by another sum of Rs.67,000/- and NC:
2023:KHC-K:5562 thereby enhance the compensation of Rs.83,000/- awarded by the Tribunal to Rs.1,50,000/-.

Since the liability of the insurer is undisputed, it shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
12. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.83,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.1,50,000/-, which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
However, the claimant is not entitled for the interest for the delayed period of 158 days in filing the appeal.

13. The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
